regions.label: Token Distribution Losses
regions.summary: How student and teacher probability distributions are compared at each generated token, including forward/reverse KL and top-k approximations.

prerequisite_links.why: Full-vocabulary KL establishes the target divergence; top-k is the practical approximation used when full vocabulary logprobs are too large.
Reverse KL changes which token IDs are selected under the top-k approximation.

side_retention_duels.prompt: In top-k distillation, which model chooses the compared token IDs?
side_retention_duels.left: Forward KL: teacher top-k token IDs
side_retention_duels.right: Reverse KL: student top-k token IDs
side_retention_duels.answer: Both are true for their respective divergence directions; the duel is about remembering which side selects the support.

quiz_questions.question: Why does TRL's distillation article approximate KL with top-k logprobs?
choices: Because full-vocabulary logprobs can require enormous tensors per sample.
Because KL cannot be computed for language models.
Because top-k changes every teacher into a smaller model.
Because vLLM only supports one token per sequence.

generative-models.label: Generative Models
generative-models.description: KL divergence, autoencoders, diffusion, likelihood models, and generation objectives.

regions.label: Knowledge Distillation & Compression
regions.summary: Teacher-student methods that transfer behavior or token distributions from large generative models into smaller deployable students.

prerequisite_links.why: Learners first compare teacher-generated trajectories with student-generated rollouts before seeing why self-generated mistakes matter.
After the training loop is clear, capacity gap explains why bigger teachers may not always produce proportionally stronger students.

side_retention_duels.prompt: Where do the training trajectories come from?
side_retention_duels.right: On-policy: student-generated rollouts scored by teacher
side_retention_duels.answer: On-policy uses the student rollouts; off-policy uses teacher-generated trajectories.

side_retention_duels.prompt: Does a much larger teacher always produce a much better student?
side_retention_duels.left: Yes, teacher benchmark gains transfer linearly
side_retention_duels.right: No, student capacity can limit absorption
side_retention_duels.answer: No. The article reports similar 4B student outcomes from 30B and 235B teachers on AIME25, suggesting a capacity gap.

quiz_questions.question: What is the core on-policy distillation move in the TRL article?
choices: Let the student generate rollouts, then ask the teacher to score those same rollouts.
Delete the teacher after generating a fixed prompt dataset.
Train only on human-written completions and avoid model logprobs.
Use a larger student than the teacher to avoid KL divergence.

regions.label: Specialized Local Students
regions.summary: Practical distillation patterns for moving useful large-model behaviors into smaller local or resource-constrained models.

prerequisite_links.why: The Qwen example is a concrete 100B+ teacher case for the broader specialized-student pattern.

side_retention_duels.prompt: Why distill instead of always using the largest teacher directly?
side_retention_duels.left: The teacher may require hundreds of GB of memory or many GPUs.
side_retention_duels.right: The student becomes larger than the teacher after training.
side_retention_duels.answer: Distillation targets deployable smaller students when the teacher is too expensive or memory-heavy to use frequently.

quiz_questions.question: Which benchmark did the Qwen math distillation section use as the main evaluation target?
choices: AIME25
ImageNet
MMLU-Pro only
HumanEval JavaScript

regions.label: Distillation Serving Systems
regions.summary: Systems patterns for making teacher-student training loops fast enough when rollout generation and teacher logprob scoring are served through inference engines.

prerequisite_links.why: The buffer exists to expose enough prompts for vLLM batching during student rollout generation.
External teacher serving creates concurrent worker requests that need batching to control tail latency.
Once server compute is fast enough, logprob payload transfer becomes the bottleneck.

side_retention_duels.prompt: What does the generation buffer decouple?
side_retention_duels.left: Training microbatch size from rollout generation batch size
side_retention_duels.right: Teacher vocabulary size from tokenizer vocabulary size
side_retention_duels.answer: It decouples training microbatch size from rollout generation batch size.

side_retention_duels.prompt: After request batching improved server latency, what became the next bottleneck?
side_retention_duels.left: Transferring top-k logprob payloads back to clients
side_retention_duels.right: Finding enough prompts in the dataset schema
side_retention_duels.answer: Logprob payload transfer became the bottleneck, motivating binary encoding.

quiz_questions.question: What format did the article use for faster teacher logprob payloads?
choices: Base64-encoded NumPy arrays containing logprobs and token IDs plus shape metadata.
Plain English JSON summaries of the teacher's reasoning.
One CSV file per generated token streamed over FTP.
A screenshot of the teacher's logits chart.

regions.label: Large Teacher Deployment Constraints
regions.summary: Memory and placement constraints that force 100B+ teacher models into separate serving infrastructure instead of colocating them with student training.

prerequisite_links.why: The 235B teacher example motivates external teacher serving because it cannot fit alongside student training.

side_retention_duels.prompt: When should a teacher move to an external server?
side_retention_duels.left: When the teacher is too large to colocate with student training GPUs
side_retention_duels.right: Whenever the student has fewer training examples
side_retention_duels.answer: External serving is motivated by teacher memory/placement constraints.

quiz_questions.question: Why did the article move 100B+ teachers to an external vLLM server?
choices: Because colocating teacher and student on the same GPUs was not practical at that scale.
Because the teacher model was a vision-only encoder.
Because JSON cannot represent text tokens.
Because on-policy distillation forbids teacher logprobs.

retrieval-augmented-generation.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
retrieval-augmented-generation.description: RAG systems, graph retrieval, corpus-grounded synthesis, query-focused summarization, and retrieval evaluation mechanisms.

router_policy.promotion_reason: GraphRAG introduced a coherent retrieval/sensemaking cluster with its own problem framing, index-building pipeline, runtime answering path, and evaluation criteria. Routing it under generic serving hid the learning path.
router_policy.future_growth_rule: Route vector RAG, GraphRAG, hybrid retrieval, reranking, indexing, query-focused summarization, and retrieval evaluation here unless the source is strictly about low-level inference serving infrastructure.

regions.label: Graph RAG & Global Sensemaking
regions.summary: How graph-structured indexes let LLMs answer corpus-wide 'sensemaking' questions that conventional chunk-retrieval RAG cannot, by summarizing communities of related entities.

prerequisite_links.why: Learners first see why similarity-retrieval RAG works for local facts, which exposes the gap on whole-corpus questions.
Once the sensemaking/QFS problem is clear, GraphRAG is introduced as the graph-based solution.
Understanding the overall approach sets up how queries are actually answered at runtime.

side_retention_duels.prompt: Which question type breaks conventional vector RAG?
side_retention_duels.left: 'What did section 3 say about X?' (local fact lookup)
side_retention_duels.right: 'What are the main themes across the whole corpus?' (global sensemaking)
side_retention_duels.answer: The global, whole-corpus sensemaking question is what vector RAG fails on, because no small set of retrieved chunks contains the answer.

side_retention_duels.prompt: Where is the single global answer assembled?
side_retention_duels.left: Map step: each community summary gives a partial answer in parallel
side_retention_duels.right: Reduce step: partial answers are combined into the final answer
side_retention_duels.answer: The reduce step combines the partial answers; the map step only produces independent partials.

quiz_questions.question: Why does GraphRAG outperform conventional vector RAG on questions like 'What are the main themes in this dataset?'
choices: Because such questions need reasoning across the whole corpus, which graph community summaries cover but a few retrieved chunks do not.
Because GraphRAG uses a larger embedding model for similarity search.
Because vector RAG cannot read text files at all.
Because GraphRAG skips the LLM and answers from the graph directly.

quiz_questions.question: What are the two stages GraphRAG uses to build its index?
choices: Derive an entity knowledge graph from source documents, then pregenerate community summaries for groups of related entities.
Fine-tune the LLM, then quantize it to 4-bit.
Crawl the web, then store embeddings in a vector database.
Translate the corpus, then deduplicate sentences.

regions.label: Graph Index Construction & Community Hierarchy
regions.summary: The pipeline that turns raw text into a queryable structure: LLM entity/relationship/claim extraction, Leiden hierarchical community detection, and bottom-up community summarization.

prerequisite_links.why: You need the entity graph before you can partition it into communities.
Communities define which elements get summarized together, bottom-up.
Once summaries drive answers, you need sensemaking-specific metrics to evaluate answer quality.

side_retention_duels.prompt: What three element kinds make up the GraphRAG index?
side_retention_duels.answer: The graph index spans nodes (entities), edges (relationships), and covariates (claims).

side_retention_duels.left: Bottom-up hierarchy: higher-level summaries fold in lower-level ones
side_retention_duels.right: A single flat summary of the whole graph at once
side_retention_duels.answer: Summaries are built bottom-up over a community hierarchy, with higher levels recursively incorporating lower-level element summaries.

quiz_questions.question: Which algorithm does GraphRAG use to partition its entity graph into nested communities?
choices: Leiden community detection, applied recursively/hierarchically.
K-means over token embeddings.
Beam search decoding.
Gradient-boosted trees.

quiz_questions.question: In GraphRAG's evaluation, what role does the 'Directness' criterion play?
choices: A control criterion expected to oppose comprehensiveness and diversity, not a target to maximize.
The primary metric GraphRAG is optimized to win.
A measure of inference latency in milliseconds.
A count of GPUs used during indexing.

GraphRAG/RAG concepts routed under LLM Systems & Serving as two new regions; consider a dedicated Retrieval & RAG cluster or macro world once more retrieval sources accumulate.
